decision.case_name: Deutsche Bank National Trust Co. v. LeTennier
decision.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
decision.retrieved_from: New York Official Reports slip opinion 2026 NY Slip Op 00040 (nycourts.gov)
decision.reported_as: Deutsche Bank Natl. Tr. Co. v LeTennier, 250 N.Y.S.3d 260 (App. Div. 3d Dept 2026)
decision.ai_tool_found: generative AI; defence counsel “reluctantly conceded during oral argument that he used AI in the preparation of his papers”
decision.scale_note: The court found at least 23 fabricated cases across five filings, plus misrepresentations of real cases. The opinion itemises only the two examples reproduced below, so this decision contributes an aggregate record plus two itemised records.

offending.as_cited: Tishman Realty & Construction Co. v Regan
offending.cited_case_name: Tishman Realty & Construction Co. v Regan
offending.reporter_citation: citation to a New York court and year given in the brief (not reproduced in the opinion)
offending.quoted_text: a proposition that “clarified” a subsection of CPLR 5015
offending.court_quote: As one example, defendant submitted the fake case name “Tishman Realty & Construction Co. v Regan,” with an accompanying citation to a New York court, year and proposition that “clarified” a subsection of CPLR 5015 — the central issue in the March 2023 order. However, the provided citation leads us to a case with a different name from Illinois, and the case name is also not found in any reported state or federal case in the United States.
offending.what_actually_exists: The reporter reference given leads to a differently named Illinois case; no reported state or federal case in the United States bears the cited name.

offending.as_cited: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. v Erobobo (127 AD3d 1176 [2d Dept 2015], lv dismissed 25 NY3d 1221 [2015])
offending.cited_case_name: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. v Erobobo
offending.quoted_text: foreclosure void where trust not properly formed
offending.court_quote: For instance, defendant submits the real case of Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. v Erobobo (127 AD3d 1176 [2d Dept 2015], lv dismissed 25 NY3d 1221 [2015]) with the false holding “foreclosure void where trust not properly formed”; the Second Department held the opposite.
offending.what_actually_exists: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. v Erobobo, 127 AD3d 1176 (2d Dept 2015) is real, and the Second Department held the opposite of the attributed holding.

offending.as_cited: [Aggregate finding] at least 23 fabricated legal authorities across five filings
offending.cited_case_name: multiple — not itemised in the opinion
offending.filing: Defendant's opening brief, opposition to the sanctions motion, reply brief and two subsequent letters to the Appellate Division
offending.court_quote: In total, defendant's five filings during this appeal include no less than 23 fabricated cases, as well as many other blatant misrepresentations of fact or law from actual cases. … Where we are most troubled is that more than half of the fake cases offered by defendant came after he was on notice of such issue, whereby his reliance on fabricated legal authorities grew more prolific as this appeal proceeded.
offending.what_actually_exists: Defendant's opening brief alone cited six cases that do not exist; the remainder accumulated across the four later filings.

controls.as_cited: Sanders v United States, 176 Fed Cl 163, 168-169 (Fed Cl 2025)
controls.cited_for: that hallucinated citations lead to cases with different names, in different courts and on different topics — or to no case at all
controls.court_quote: Hallucinated cases may look like a real case because they include familiar-looking reporter information, but their citations lead to cases with different names, in different courts and on different topics — or even to no case at all (see Sanders v United States, 176 Fed Cl 163, 168-169 [Fed Cl 2025]).
